title: Kenyan Lamb Rack
community: Urban Kenya — the luxury hotel fine dining dish
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Lamb Rack — a frenched rack of lamb crusted with Kenyan herbs, pan-seared to a perfect crust, and oven-roasted to a blushing medium-rare. The premium fine dining protein — elegant, precise, and spectacular on the plate.
longDesc: Lamb rack is the hallmark of a confident kitchen — it requires precise timing, cannot be rushed, and reveals the cook's skill immediately on the plate. At Nairobi's finest hotels, a properly executed lamb rack is a statement dish.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh coriander and parsley — mixed
½ cup red wine or stock
steps: Process herbs, garlic, breadcrumbs, and oil into a coarse paste.
Season lamb with salt and pepper.
Sear fat-side down in a very hot pan for 4 minutes until deeply golden.
Remove from heat. Brush with Dijon mustard. Press herb crust firmly onto the fat cap.
Roast at 200°C for 10—12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 55—57°C (medium-rare).
Rest 8 minutes — the temperature will rise to 60°C.
Make jus: deglaze pan with wine and stock. Reduce by half. Whisk in butter.
Slice into double cutlets. Serve with jus.
chefTips: A thermometer is essential — lamb rack is too expensive to overcook.
The rest period is as important as the cook — it redistributes juices throughout the meat.
French the bones cleanly — they are part of the visual impact of this dish.
commonMistakes: No thermometer — guessing with expensive lamb is too risky.
Overcooking — well-done lamb rack is a tragedy.
cookingScience: Lamb fat melts at a higher temperature than chicken or pork fat (around 43°C vs 35—36°C) — this is why searing the fat cap first is more important with lamb. The rendered fat bastes the meat as it drips. At 55—57°C, the muscle proteins are just set — the meat is tender and blush-pink. Beyond 70°C, the proteins over-contract and the meat becomes dry and grey.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan lamb from highland farms — supporting local smallholder pastoralists.
reheating: Warm gently in oven — never microwave.
healthBenefits: Rich in B12, zinc, and iron.
culturalNote: Lamb rack represents Kenya's hotel industry reaching for international fine dining standards — a dish that competes with any served in London, Paris, or New York, using Kenya's own quality lamb.
